newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: World Bank approves $46 million loan for S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: World Bank approves $46 million loan for S.Africa.

text.p: The directors of the World Bank have approved a loan for $46 million to South Africa to help fund industrial competitiveness and job creation programmes, South Africa's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said on Friday.
The loan falls within South Africa's existing borrowing limit and is designed to improve and diversify the government's foreign debt portfolio, the DTI said in a statement.
The loan will be allocated to three programmes developed by the DTI with the first two elements to be launched later this year when management programmes are in place.

- The Competitiveness Fund: a matching grant fund to firms operating in South Africa which will allow them to make use of specialised advice from business service organisations such as marketing and technical consultants, with the government contributing 50 percent of the approved costs;

- The Sector Partnership Fund: a fund designed to allow groups of firms or industrial organisations to seek collective solutions to their technical, marketing or strategic problems, with the governent contributing 65 percent of approved costs;

- The Short-Term Export Finance Guarantee Facility: an extension of a DTI programme launched in November 1996, providing guarantees to banks lending to small and medium firms to finance their export orders.
